concerns.text: The plan uses a single stratified 80/20 train‑test split (random_state=42) without any cross‑validation or repeated sampling. This makes the reported AUC, precision, and recall highly dependent on one random split and risks over‑estimating predictive performance.

Class imbalance is not addressed. The distribution of pass/fail labels in SWE‑Gym / Multi‑SWE‑RL is unknown, yet no re‑sampling, class weighting, or metric adjustment (e.g., balanced accuracy) is described, which can bias the classifier and inflate performance metrics.

The feature vector schema includes a `language` field, but the modeling description does not incorporate language as a predictor nor stratify analyses by language. Language is a potential confound (Python vs C++ may have different static‑dynamic relationships) and should be controlled for.

When memory limits force a fallback to a 10 % stratified sample, no power analysis is provided. The plan merely notes that “the report will note reduced statistical power,” but does not quantify the effect on detectable effect sizes or confidence intervals, risking under‑powered conclusions.
